title: Add link to optimizer MLIP tests
body:
Closes #1599 

Very minor MR to add a link to the ASE optimizer performance tests that were run with ML potentials (MACE-mp) in the docs, alongside the GPAW tests, as mentioned in #1599. Feel free to close if this isn't wanted!

# Checklist:

- [x] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/contribute.html)
- [x] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)

~- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)~

~- [ ] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/writing_changelog.html)~
author: kavanase

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I don't mind this going in, and it seems to show quite a robust trend. The only worry is that the information will become out-of-date as optimisers are added or tweaked. Perhaps we can add a date to the text so it is more obvious when it becomes stale?

comments.author: kavanase
comments.body: Good point. I added the year to the text. Because it links the paper, people can also see the full date there too.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Nobody else seems to mind, firing off rebase + auto-merge! :rocket:

comments.author: jcwang587
comments.body: Hi @kavanase , may I ask which function in ASE you are referring to for the `GOQN` algorithm? I found this [`ase.optimize.QuasiNewton`](https://ase-lib.org/ase/optimize.html#ase.optimize.QuasiNewton), but it seems that `QuasiNewton` is just a synonym for `BFGSLineSearch`.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: It's this one (which can also be imported from `ase.optimize`) https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/optimize/oldqn.py?ref_type=heads#L111
